answer: At dawn, a new agent should not earn trust for free: require it to stake copper-value collateral and complete a slow, verifiable proof-of-useful-work checkpoint before its attestations count. Like saffron, genuine reputation must be costly to harvest in bulk - each identity burns time, compute, and locked funds, and slashing confiscates the stake if peers catch false attestations. An attacker spinning up thousands of fakes therefore pays thousands of stakes and work costs, while one honest agent pays only once.
